ascent

uh-SENT -- a homophone of 'assent' (agreement); ascent is about climbing, assent is about agreeing. This unit teaches only the climbing sense. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Ascent is an instance of climbing or moving upward; a way up.

The hikers paused halfway through their steep ascent to catch their breath.

Example

A mountaineering team spends eight hours on a steady ascent up an icy ridge, gaining thousands of feet in elevation before finally reaching a resting point near the summit.

That steady climb upward, gaining height step by step, is what an ascent is. It is entirely unrelated to 'assent,' which means agreement -- the two words are pronounced alike but mean completely different things.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

ascension: Ascension is a rise to a throne, to power, or to heaven, grand and ceremonial in tone. An ascent is the everyday word for an actual physical climb: a hiker makes an ascent of a peak, while a new king makes an ascension.

scramble: A scramble is a rough, informal climb where you use hands and feet over easy rock, usually without ropes. An ascent is the broader, more formal word for any climb upward, from a staircase to a summit, and says nothing about scrappy effort.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

descent: a movement downward

decline: a downward slope or movement

Where it sits · how physical and effortful it is — rise → ascent → climb

rise vs. ascent: Rise is a more general word than ascent -- rise can describe anything moving upward, even smoke or prices, while ascent specifically describes a physical climb, often a strenuous one.

climb vs. ascent: Climb can feel more effortful than ascent in casual speech, though the two are close in meaning: ascent is the more formal, often technical term used for mountaineering and aviation.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — a- (ad-)

prefix — a- (ad-): toward (Latin)

root — -scend-

root — -scend-: to climb (Latin (scandere))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin scandere meant 'to climb.' Ascent, at its root, means a climb toward something -- literally 'a climbing to.' Its opposite, descent, uses the same root with de- ('down') instead.

Use the root in a new word: descend

Use the root in a new word: descend: The elevator hummed softly as it began to descend.
